title: The Kate Smith show: every section must be heard
summary: The show demanded sixteen bars featuring every brass and sax player, and he admits he was an unsuccessful radio orchestrator.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: The same thing would happen on the Kate Smith Show, which I did for three years. I remember one time changing what they wanted -- you know, what they wanted was Kate Smith sings the first chorus, and then for 16 bars you've got to bring the orchestra in, and they had four trumpets, four trombones. They had five saxophones, and they wanted them all, whether it was in -- whether it was all harmonized out, and they had guys like Charlie Margolis and -- and the guy that used to play -- play out in Detroit with us occasionally, a
good friend of Bix's Vic, Nat Natoli. And they had Russ Case and Andy Secress.
So they figured they're paying for all those instruments, they want to hear them.
"I want to hear" One each -- one by one --
They would count every part. Now then, we had trombones under there with Jack Jenny and Buddy Morrow and several other guys that could really belt it out, and those guys stood up.
We used to do this in a theater down on 46th Street, and they used to stand up and just blow it out. And you had to do that for 16 bars.
Then she'd come back in on the bridge, huh?
Then she'd come back in. And that -- that was the whole arrangement.

I remember Jack gave me -- Jack Miller, who had the band -- he gave me five of those things to do one week, and, you know, it could have meant demand a little money. I couldn't get -- maybe -- I think I got three, maybe four or five, squeezing, you know.
